cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Fair Exchange
cards.instruction: Price every favor in time, effort, inconvenience, or future obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. Half an hour helping you move buys two hours painting my shed on Saturday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Saturday's my only lie-in. Can I come after lunch?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. Afternoon painting costs me cricket. Three hours, then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hire a painter. But I need the sofa carried up three flights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then two painter-hours covers loading; the stairs cost a third. Cricket's free again.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 wrappers do not add specific estimating expertise, while painting hours and cricket costs clearly price favors.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 afternoon request causes A3 extra cricket cost; B4 hired painter and stairs cause A5 revised labour price.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects a lie-in and B4 offers paid substitution while naming the real move, making negotiation meaningful.

heightening.evidence: A5 separates stair cost from loading and welcomes returned cricket time after B4 solution.

specificity.evidence: A1 time exchange and B4 three flights define the work and its change.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 unnamed standard clutters the otherwise concrete inconvenience calculation.
